memory_candidates.content: A gitignore file placed at a subdirectory (e.g. specs/.gitignore) gives a **/-prefixed pattern full coverage relative to that subdirectory, including at its own root -- **/.sessions/ inside specs/.gitignore ignores specs/.sessions/ directly, not just nested occurrences. This can close an ignore-coverage gap previously believed to require the repo-root .gitignore, when the only blocker was the delivery mechanism (e.g. a deploy pipeline that can only write into a different directory), not gitignore's own matching semantics. Verify with a live git check-ignore -v probe before assuming a subdirectory .gitignore can't reach a pattern.

When adding a new member to a hand-indexed parallel-array pattern library (id/pattern/probe/regex/flag arrays kept in lockstep by index), grep every consumer test for a hardcoded count assertion (e.g. `[[ "$id_count" -eq 16 ]]`) before declaring the change complete -- a suite that asserts an exact class-membership count will silently break even though the library's own internal consistency (all arrays same length) still holds, and this class of companion-file breakage is easy to miss since it's not listed in a plan's own Files-to-modify enumeration.
